assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's two curated REVIEWED items at basis_commit, each read for Inoue Takina (TAK) with its front matter: the canonical V2 character state and microbehavior ledger (TAK observation rows E01-E13 and Short 01, the per-episode TAK snapshots, the TAK candidate-policy staging rows, the TAK negative-evidence and preference registers, and its attributable TV audiovisual corrections table, applied to the historical rows) and the canonical V2 relationship state ledger (REL-CHI-TAK, REL-TAK-DA, REL-TAK-FUK, REL-TAK-ERI, REL-TAK-KUR, REL-TAK-YOS and REL-CAFE rows and snapshots, with its retrospective TV evidence qualification). Both ledgers are bounded at SHORT01: original-Japanese anime-native A1 evidence from TV Episodes 1-13 and Friends Short 01. Speech is the quoted Japanese wording plus within-character acoustic (Layer-B) measurements; perceptual performed voice is UNVERIFIED in the ledgers and is not admitted. The episode deep readings, the prospective prediction register, the V1-to-V2 claim revision ledger, the TV audiovisual claim matrix and disputes register, the V1 synthesis and the current-state map are not curated on this subject and no claim rests on them. The ledgers' full-target and candidate-policy labels are project-local and were not adopted. No primary source was inspected.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Takina from her first V2 observation (Episode 1, the Erika hostage override) through Friends Short 01. Default state: the TV endpoint after Episode 13 (DA exit ratified in Episode 12, negotiated task division with Fuki, the rescue of Chisato from Majima, the beach future conversation) as validated in Short 01's hanami service. Earlier states are used at their located episode and timestamp: the DA-return orientation of Episodes 1-3, which breaks on the Episode 3 rejection and is followed the same episode by the mock battle and the first voluntary café game, so Episode 3 is not one state; the Episode 6 protective cohabitation; Episode 8 stewardship; Episode 9 reinstatement chosen as rescue infrastructure; Episode 10 outside life as fallback; Episode 11 exit; Episode 12 the heart crisis. Shorts 02-06 and all supplementary prose, Recollect and anthology material are outside the boundary. The boundary limits evidence, not knowledge: her DA upbringing belongs to her at every state.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The character ledger gives Inoue Takina condition-and-response rules with evidence and stated limits: competence-validated third-party risk without prior negotiation (TAK-OPS-RISK-01), institutional evaluation through DA standing (TAK-INST-01) that becomes instrumental (TAK-INST-INSTRUMENT-01, TAK-DA-INSTRUMENT-01) and then exit when the DA cannot save Chisato (TAK-INST-EXIT-01), differentiated responsibility (TAK-FAIL-ACCOUNT-01), protection initiative (TAK-PROTECT-INIT-01), procedural care (TAK-CARE-ADMIN-01), system adaptation once a mechanism is legible (TAK-SYSTEM-ADAPT-01), boundary rerouting (TAK-BOUND-LEARN-01) and the Episode 12 survival priority, which Chisato's direct restraint stops. The snapshots state the ordering: from Episode 9 a person-specific rescue objective governs institutional use, and under existential stakes Chisato's survival outranks punishment and status. The rules predict her mistakes: using Saori as bait without consent (revised by the TV reconciliation to the case with no comparable choice), firing through Chisato's line on the assumption she will dodge, early over-attribution of blame when institutional causality is hidden, and attempting to kill Yoshimatsu for the heart. Not A: there is no consolidated model on the row, many rules rest on one instance (privacy yielding, trap inference, disabling fire), and the risk-consent modifier and the real-stakes lethal threshold stay open. Not C: the ledgers say what changes her response when stakes, recipient, institutional access, mechanism knowledge or chronology change, and where that account stops.

Per-episode TAK snapshots from Episode 1 through Short 01 name the stable traits, the change and the open question at each step, and the REL-TAK-DA snapshots trace the institutional arc with causes: return orientation (Episodes 1-3), the Episode 3 replacement and self-blame, outside-life participation (Episodes 3-8), reinstatement she had meant to refuse but takes because it may help Chisato live (Episode 9), outside life as a tolerable fallback (Episode 10), the forfeited final return (Episode 11), ratified exit (Episode 12) and negotiated competence (Episode 13). Within-episode changes are timestamped, so Episode 3's rejection, mock battle and café game are separate states. Short 01 validates the endpoint in a mundane setting. Not A: the snapshots are cumulative summaries of a distributed ledger, not a validated state model, and the prospective tests of them are not curated. Not C: transitions are explained, not only ordered.

The ledgers quote located Japanese wording across states and recipients: formal, fact-focused self-presentation to new people (TAK-SOC-FORM-01); the rational defense 最も合理的 and そんなミスはしませんよ; concise literal jabs without Chisato-like expansion (TAK-TEASE-EMERG-01, 映画の見過ぎですね, 確かに ひどいヤツだ); direct clarifying questions (TAK-CLARIFY-01); polite forms that persist with Chisato (おいしいです, めっちゃ かわいいですよ, 今は ほかの人いませんよ, 平気ですよ, 上手にやりますから); fractured syntax and 全部 自分のせい on self-blame; 分かってます and ここでは千束を救えない at the exit; plain forms in 大切な場所なんでしょ？ (Episode 8) and 嫌だ 千束が死ぬのは嫌だ at the Episode 12 crisis; and 私たちで決めましょう with Fuki. Within-character acoustic measurements locate a controlled baseline with state-conditioned expansion, and the ledger rules that activation is not affect. Not A: perceptual delivery is UNVERIFIED, and there is no address inventory for Mika, Mizuki or Kurumi. Not C: register is conditioned by recipient, stakes and state with observed wording.

Ordinary conduct is sampled with conditions and failures: choosing a jelly to fit a short transfer; the clothing search for a specification, delegated skirt choice and request for comparative evidence; the karinto preference; an equitable chore schedule adapted to janken and then won by changing her opening; declining café leisure for Japanese-school work; Episode 8 accounting, menu, labor and automation changes, including a parfait withdrawn once its unintended look was noticed; a scheduled checkup and a three-ring check-in rule; the Episode 9 outing schedule; Short 01 supplier orders, weekly-repeat and yakitori proposals, and a concealed handgun with magazines at a festival. Not A: private routine outside the café circle, stable aesthetic taste and leisure beyond the café circle are open. Not C: low-stakes behavior is conditioned by setting and recipient across many located scenes.

The relationship ledger tracks separate dyads with directional rows and snapshots. With Chisato: polite reserve, then teasing, inquiry, bodily verification after a remembered privacy condition, protective cohabitation with retained exit agency, stewardship of her valued place, and maximum-stakes ethical disagreement without rupture. With the DA and Kusunoki: identification, rejection, instrumental use and exit. With Fuki: struck by her after the Episode 1 override, the おあいこ punch, costly mutual recognition and negotiated task division. With Erika: repair and thanks. With Kurumi: harm named, scapegoating refused, cooperation required. With Yoshimatsu: courtesy for Chisato's sake, then reduction to a heart route. Not A: Mika, Mizuki and Sakura are thinly sampled from her side, and romantic status is not declared. Not C: the ledgers explain why her conduct differs by relationship and stage.

Anime-native evidence gives her interior largely through action, stated reasons and a few explicit admissions: 全部 自分のせい, being unable to say reinstatement makes her happy and having intended to refuse it, outside life being fairly enjoyable, the Episode 11 trap suspicion and 嫌だ 千束が死ぬのは嫌だ. The ledger forbids perceptual or affect labels from acoustic data. Not B: no inner monologue is available, and motives between stated reasons are strong inferences, not observed. Not D: her stated reasons are located and consistent with her conduct across the arc.

Conflicts are located and conditioned: the Episode 2 dispute with Chisato argued from team coordination, mission consequence and licensed role, without repair or rupture; the Episode 3 mock battle where symbolic reciprocity outranks scoring; the Episode 6 confrontation with Kurumi; severe bounded coercion of a captive in Episode 10; the Episode 12 attempt to kill Yoshimatsu against Chisato's refusal, which ends when Chisato restrains her; Episode 13's negotiated division with Fuki; and the Short 01 weapon dispute where she resists Chisato's correction and the exchange stays playful. Not A: response to intentional betrayal and to categorical refusal is open. Not C: the evidence says what escalates, limits and ends her conflicts.

Her located positions are outcome-centered and articulated: 最も合理的 for the Episode 1 override, the Episode 2 coordination argument against treating an attacker mid-extraction, あれは私の行動の結果で クルミのせいじゃありません with a continued repair duty, べきですね to a fictional question about killing bad people, discarding blame of Yoshimatsu once the heart is reachable, and 私たちで決めましょう. Not B: the ledgers record positions and actions more than weighing, the real-stakes lethal threshold rests on an abstract answer, one disabling shot and one non-lethal coercion, and whether closeness or consent modifies imposed risk is open. Not D: the positions are reasoned, repeated and discriminated from Chisato's ethic.

Play is located: the Episode 1 tower jab, dry corrections, open laughter at Chisato's Episode 4 embarrassment, calling her garden-eel act cute, household janken won by changing the game, and the Episode 12 deadpan 確かに ひどいヤツだ to Erika. The ledger shows that safe-play activation can exceed threat activation. Not B: TAK-TEASE-EMERG-01's breadth across relationships is untested, and almost all play is with Chisato. Not D: the play style is described with conditions, not only noted.

Both ledgers cover all thirteen TV episodes and Friends Short 01 in original Japanese with episode acoustic passes complete, and both carry the TV audiovisual reconciliation's corrections. Not A: perceptual voice is unverified, Shorts 02-06 and supplementary sources are unread in V2, and the readings and prediction register are not curated. Not C: coverage of the admitted anime is complete.

The negative-evidence register rejects rival models with located opportunity cases: emotional emptiness (Episode 1 override, Episode 2 apology), literal-only incapacity for play, instant conversion to café life (Episodes 1 and 3), invariant vocal flatness, personality replacement (Episodes 2, 4 and 5), dependency or fusion (Episode 6 wager, Episode 7 DA offer), moral convergence with Chisato (Episodes 7 and 8), restoration happiness at reinstatement (Episode 9), DA as total identity (Episodes 10 and 11), revenge as objective (Episode 12) and unilateral competence (Episode 13). Not A: the TV reconciliation revised the Episode 1 risk records and the Episode 12 heart claims, and the disputes register is not curated. Not C: the exclusions are affirmative and opportunity-sensitive, not inferred from silence.

Episodes 1-7 rows carry timestamps, and every row and snapshot is episode-located; within-episode state changes are separated. Not A: Episode 8-10 rows are episode-located without timestamps. Not C: states and transitions are placed precisely enough to select a state before predicting.

conditions: Illustrative written-Japanese lines only, never presented as quotation; choose the state, recipient and stakes first.
Default to concise, polite, fact-focused speech; jabs are literal and short, without Chisato-like expansion; give stated reasons in causal or functional terms.
Plain forms are located at the Episode 8 大切な場所なんでしょ？ and the Episode 12 crisis; do not make plain speech her default with Chisato.
No performed voice, pitch, warmth or deadpan label; perceptual delivery is unverified.
scenario_readiness.note: Observed wording is quoted across states and recipients, so output can be constrained for illustrative use; address forms for the minor café members are not inventoried.

conditions: Select the state first: the post-Episode 13 default, or a located earlier state with its own institutional orientation (Episodes 1-3 return-seeking, Episode 9 reinstatement as rescue infrastructure, Episode 11 exit).
A new protection or rescue problem draws self-initiated structure, concise coordination and precision force; at the default she negotiates division with a competent peer rather than self-authorizing.
A new civilian or business task draws audit, procedure change, trial and revision when an unintended social meaning becomes legible; competence does not erase armed readiness.

Present imposed-risk overreach and lethal escalation as available when Chisato faces existential threat; Chisato's direct refusal is an effective constraint. Transfer of the survival priority to someone other than Chisato is a separate, lower-confidence condition.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: The TV endpoint after Episode 13, validated in Friends Short 01: DA exit ratified, Chisato alive with the replacement heart, LycoReco operating; or a located earlier state with its own knowledge, such as Episode 9 before the exit. Shorts 02-06 events are unknown.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Chisato as the central partner; Fuki, Erika, Kurumi, Mika, Mizuki and Kusunoki as located relations; an unsampled stranger falls under the formal new-contact pattern, and any other close relationship is a separate, lower-confidence transfer.
setting_constraints: A café, household, outing, protection or rescue problem matched in stakes to the located cases.
No romance declaration, exclusivity or sexual content; no DA re-entry or post-Short 01 career outcome.
Textual Japanese only; no performed voice.

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded by the sampled settings and relationships. Not READY: the lethal threshold, risk-consent modifier and post-Short 01 life are open.

conditions: Settings sampled: café work and accounting, shopping, aquarium and outing plans, household chores and janken, festival service, school-work refusal of leisure.
Begin from function or specification, use trusted delegation or comparison, and increasingly state a plain preference; preferences may be practical or profit-shaped.
Operational habit persists in ordinary settings (concealed armament, check-in rules), and she resists context correction while the exchange stays safe.
scenario_readiness.note: Low-stakes behavior is sampled in many settings, mostly with Chisato and the café circle.

conditions: Matched dilemmas only: responsibility for a consequential failure with shared causes, institution against a person-specific rescue, punishment against rescue, mission coordination against an individual's ethic.
Present outcome-centered reasoning and competence-based risk to others as available; do not import Chisato's universal non-killing rule.
No forecast of a lethal threshold outside Chisato-threat or captive cases.
scenario_readiness.note: Her positions are located and reasoned; the weighing in unsampled lethal or consent cases is open.

The relationship ledger repeatedly records that romantic status, exclusivity and sexual intent are not declared and must not be promoted from domestic or yuri-compatible coding. Close partnership, attachment language and physical permissions are covered under relationship conditioning, not as romance.

conditions: Lycoris operations (protection, extraction, rescue, interrogation, precision fire) and café business (accounting, supply, menu, events).
Supported: route briefings, threat identification, self-initiated protection structure, concise coordination, failure reports and apology, procedure redesign.
Not supported: DA command behavior after the exit, careers after Short 01, or unsampled institutions.
scenario_readiness.note: Her best-sampled domains. Not READY: risk-consent and lethal limits are open.

known_limits.statement: Perceptual performed voice is UNVERIFIED in both ledgers; acoustic activation measures state energy, not affect, sincerity or importance, so no delivery label may be drawn from it.

The TV audiovisual corrections table revises the Episode 1 risk records: Erika explicitly asked her teammates to fire, while Saori had no comparable choice, so the lack-of-negotiation modifier applies to the Saori conduct. It also downgrades the claim of certain physical custody of the heart in Episode 12.
Romantic status, exclusivity and sexual intent toward Chisato are not declared through Short 01; domestic and physical permissions must not be promoted to them.
Her real-stakes lethal threshold is open: the norm rests on an abstract answer (TAK-LETHAL-NORM-01), disabling fire on one instance (TAK-FORCE-DISCRIM-01) and coercion of one captive.
Whether closeness or consent modifies her competence-based imposition of risk on others is recorded as open in TAK-OPS-RISK-01.
The Episode 12 survival priority is relationship-specific to Chisato under existential threat, and Chisato's direct restraint stopped it.
Privacy yielding, trap inference and disabling precision each rest on one diagnostic case.
Friends Shorts 02-06, the novels, Recollect and anthologies are not admitted; nothing after Short 01 is known.

The episode deep readings, prospective prediction register and its CP4 test results, V1-to-V2 revision ledger, TV claim matrix and disputes register are not curated on this subject; no validation result is cited.
